newsitem.title: USA: News Corp, IFE close to deal - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: News Corp, IFE close to deal - WSJ.

text.p: News Corp Ltd is getting closer to cutting a $1 billion deal to buy International Family Entertainment Corp, the Wall Street Journal said.
However, in Wednesday's electronic edition, the Journal said the negotiations may hit a snag over demands by the Robertson family, which controls IFE.
IFE owns the Family Channel, a cable channel. News Corp has been hoping to buy IFE to broadcast its children's programming.
Unnamed sources close to the matter told the Journal that News Corp has proposed buying the whole company, which has more than 47 million fully diluted shares.
The Journal said a potential killer snag is that the Robertson family, who are Class A shareholders, are seeking a premium price.
IFE has two classes of stock and the Journal said other holders are upset since they believe the company's articles of incorporation call for all holders to be treated equally.

People close to the negotiations said News Corp recently proposed paying between $26 and $28 a share for the Class B shares, of which Liberty Media Corp owns about 23 percent. The Robertsons recently lowered their sights to $40 a share from $70 a share, the Journal said.

Meanwhile, IFE investor Mario Gabelli said he intends to withhold from voting his shares in its annual meeting because of concerns about the company's lack of disclosure of talks with News Corp, as well as the structure of the proposed agreement.
